name: Yaesu FT-270R
notes: Stock, unmodified FT-270R: a 2 m submersible handheld (~2007). Not to be confused with the unrelated 1980s FT-270R/FT-270RH 25 W mobile; if a spec sheet says 25 W or 13.8 VDC it is the mobile. Bench-verified 2026-09-13 against a physical radio (Chicago-Offline ft270-277-info, dumps/ft270r-2026-09-13-read.md): the radio reports model ID 'AH022$', so stock CHIRP programs it as a Yaesu VX-170 with no patch, and the clone image is the FT-7800-family format at 6057 bytes with valid checksums. Channel storage limits are the driver's (chirp/drivers/vx170.py, which inherits ft7800.FTx800Radio): max_channels 200 is memory_bounds (1, 200) and the memory[200] struct, matching the published 200-memory figure; max_channel_name_chars 6 is the names[200] struct with char name[6]. Those six-character alphanumeric tags are far shorter than any of our Chinese radios, so display names need aggressive shortening. modes is ["FM"]: the driver declares MODES ["FM", "NFM"] and has no AM; bandwidths_khz 12.5/25 follows that split. The TX band is the US amateur 2 m allocation 144-148 MHz; the wider 137-174 MHz span is the driver's valid_bands and is rx_only because stock firmware will not transmit outside the ham band. If this radio is ever MARS/CAP-modded, add a separate radio id for it the way yaesu_ft277_mars does, rather than widening TX here. max_zones is 1 as a profile-0.1 compatibility shim: the VX-170 driver sets has_bank = False, so memory banks are not reachable through the CHIRP path even though the chassis has them. Write path: CHIRP.app GUI upload (verified on the FT-277R sibling, same clone protocol); cable is the RT Systems CT57B at 9600 baud.
